    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    Eczema, also known as Atopic Dermatitis, is a common, chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes dry, red, and intensely itchy patches. 
    Symptoms
    • Intense itchiness (pruritus) that often worsens at night
    • Dry, cracked, scaly, or leathery skin
    • Red to brownish-gray patches, commonly on the hands, feet, ankles, wrists, neck, upper chest, and inside the bends of the elbows and knees
    • Small, raised bumps that may leak fluid and crust over when scratched 
    Causes and Triggers
    • Genetics: A family history of eczema, asthma, or hay fever increases risk. 
    • Immune dysfunction:
      An overactive immune response reacts to environmental triggers.
       
    • Irritants: Soaps, detergents, fragrances, wool, and synthetic fabrics. 
    • Allergens: Dust mites, pet dander, pollen, and mold. 
    • Environmental factors: Dry air, extreme heat or cold, and sweat. 
    • Stress: Emotional stress can provoke or worsen flare-ups. 
    Treatments and Management
    • Moisturizing: Apply thick creams or The National Eczema Association approved ointments daily, ideally right after a warm (not hot) 10-minute bath. 
    • Topical medications: Over-the-counter or prescription creams, such as topical corticosteroids or calcineurin inhibitors, to reduce inflammation. 
    • Trigger avoidance: Identify and eliminate personal irritants and allergens from your environment. 
    • Oral medications or light therapy: Used for severe cases that do not respond to topical care. 
    If you'd like, let me know:
    • Who is experiencing the symptoms (an infant, child, or adult)?
    • Where the rash is located on the body?
    I can provide more tailored skin care or management strategies.

    What is eczema caused by?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview

    AI Mode replied:

    Eczema is caused by a combination of genetics, a weakened skin barrier, immune system overactivity, and environmental triggers. 
    While there is no single direct cause, doctors and scientists understand that these key factors work together to create the condition: 
    Key Underlying Factors
    • Genetics: Eczema often runs in families. If your parents have eczema, asthma, or hay fever, you are more likely to get it. 
    • Skin Barrier Dysfunction: Many people with eczema have a mutation in the gene that makes filaggrin. Filaggrin is a protein that helps keep your skin strong and hydrated. Without enough of it, the skin loses moisture easily. 
    • Immune System Overactivity: A weak skin barrier lets outside substances in. Your immune system mistakes these harmless substances for threats and overreacts, creating inflammation that leads to red, itchy skin
      .
       
    Common Flare-Up Triggers
    While not the root cause, these external factors can wake up the immune response and cause a flare-up: 
    • Irritants: Soaps, detergents, shampoos, fragrances, and household cleaners.
    • Allergens: Dust mites, pollen, mold, and pet dander.
    • Weather: Very dry, hot, or cold air, as well as rapid changes in temperature.
    • Microbes: Bacteria like Staphylococcus aureus living on the skin can worsen inflammation.
    • Stress: Emotional stress can make the itch-scratch cycle much worse. 
    If you or someone you know is dealing with eczema, let me know:
    • Where the rash is located
    • What triggers seem to make it worse
    I can share tips on how to manage symptoms and protect your skin barrier.
